---
title: "Lead-time test"
subtitle: "Do US-reported imports say something about an economy's exports before its own figure is out?"
---

```{python}
import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import Markdown
from itables import init_notebook_mode, show

from pdi import site

init_notebook_mode(connected=False)

lead, meta = site.load("trade", "lead_test")
finding = meta.get("finding")
ran = bool(meta.get("test_ran"))
```

The United States publishes its imports about five weeks after a month ends. The export
figures of the Southeast Asian economies reach the international tables one to five months
later. If US imports from an economy move with that economy's total exports, the US figure
is an early reading. This page tests that claim, with rules
[written before any trade figure was collected](../methodology.qmd#trade-and-supply-chain).

## Verdict

```{python}
#| output: asis
if not ran:
    print(site.empty_state(meta, "Lead-time test"))
else:
    passed = lead[lead["passes"] == True]
    if passed.empty:
        print('::: {.verdict}\n**No signal found.** For none of the six economies did adding US '
              'imports beat the baseline by more than twice the standard error of the gain. The '
              'claim is dropped and nothing on this site uses US imports as an early reading.\n:::\n')
    else:
        print(f'::: {{.verdict}}\n**The claim holds for {", ".join(passed["name"])}** and is '
              f'dropped for the others.\n:::\n')
    print(site.finding_line(finding))
```

## The test, economy by economy

The target is the year-on-year growth of the economy's total goods exports. The baseline is
last month's growth. The model adds the year-on-year growth of US imports from the economy
in the same month. Both are scored on the months after the fitting period; errors are in
percentage points of growth.

```{python}
if ran:
    cols = {"name": "Economy", "train_months": "Months fitted", "test_months": "Months scored",
            "mae_baseline": "Baseline error", "mae_model": "Model error", "gain": "Gain",
            "gain_se": "Standard error of gain", "verdict": "Verdict"}
    t = lead[[c for c in cols if c in lead.columns]].rename(columns=cols).round(2)
    show(t, paging=False, showIndex=False, classes="display compact")
```

## How the two growth rates line up

The correlation between the economy's export growth and the growth of US imports from it,
with the US figure shifted by up to three months. A negative shift pairs each month's exports
with a later month of US imports; a positive shift with an earlier one. A peak at a positive
shift would mean the US figure moves first.

```{python}
#| output: asis
if ran:
    shifts = [c for c in lead.columns if c.startswith("corr_shift_")]
    t = lead[["name", *shifts]].rename(
        columns={"name": "Economy", **{c: c.replace("corr_shift_", "") + " months" for c in shifts}}
    ).round(2)
    print(f'{site.finding_badge({"label": "observation"})} Correlations are arithmetic on the '
          f'published figures; they are not the test.\n')
    show(t, paging=False, showIndex=False, classes="display compact")
print("\n## Sources and limits\n")
print(site.source_note(meta))
print("\nThis product uses the Census Bureau Data API but is not endorsed or certified by the "
      "Census Bureau.")
```
